Chrome 154 silently ignores --load-extension; load unpacked extensions via the CDP browser-target command Extensions.loadUnpacked({path}) instead.

Chrome 154.0.8037.93 starts normally with --load-extension and the flag does NOTHING — no error, no warning. The only extension service workers present are Chrome's own built-ins, so a harness that attaches to 'the service worker' silently measures a Google extension (observed: fignfifoniblkonapihmkfakmlgkbkcf, reporting metricsPrivate/offscreen permissions and no chrome.webRequest) and then reports a meaningless failure. --enable-unsafe-extension-debugging does not fix it.

Working path: connect to the websocket from /json/version and call Extensions.loadUnpacked({path}); it returns the new extension's id, and chrome-extension://<id>/background.js then appears in /json/list.

Verified by spike/probe-load.mjs on 2026-10-02: A(--load-extension)=false, B(+unsafe flag)=false, C(CDP loadUnpacked)=true. Re-run 'task spike:probe-load' if a future Chrome changes this.
